bugs.error_message: P12 cutout pin diverged: Rust Simplex.cutout_from_simplex produced 7 pieces vs oracle 5 (corners 1/2 got 2 zero-length division lines instead of 1)
root_cause: Simplex.calcDivisionLines mixes TWO Java Direction-comparison flavors, and the port initially conflated them. (1) The NULL guards use reference equality: currentProjectionDir == Direction.NULL is true only for the shared constant that Point.perpendicularDirection returns in its collinear branch; translating that as == on IntDirection failed because IntDirection PartialEq mirrors Java .equals (collinear side + positive projection) under which distinct NULL instances are UNEQUAL — so the zero direction never matched and the guards never fired (the original 7-vs-5 piece divergence). (2) The final comparison Simplex.java:1137 is firstProjectionDir.equals(secondProjectionDir) — VALUE equality, NOT reference ==; an interim fix translated it as an object-identity flag, which was a misreading (caught in the Task 7 spec review): an identity flag diverges from .equals whenever the two directions are value-equal but distinct objects, which is reachable with raw parallel same-direction outer line pairs.
fix: NULL guards now use IntDirection::is_null() (zero-vector check; sound because the shared constant is the only zero direction those call sites can produce). The final comparison is plain Rust first_projection_dir == second_projection_dir, which IS Java .equals (T9 contract). Oracle pin PB9 (raw outer simplex with a duplicated same-direction bottom line, sharp inner triangle corner (4,0)) drives the second-division scan through the value-equal twin and pins the 2-division-line outcome.

bugs.error_message: Corpus cases seg-000020/000093/000125 (line_segment.sort_endpoints_in_xy) and seg-000151 (line_segment.intersection) mismatched: Rust serialized {"kind":"RustPanic"} where the Java oracle produced a sorted LineSegment / a 1-cut LineList.

The Rust port instead panicked at start_point/end_point (precondition the oracle does not have) and skipped the parallel candidate in border_intersections (a documented Task-6 divergence). Confirmed via jshell: seg-000020 sp = RationalPoint(822986573811360, 822986573811360, 0), seg-000093 sp = RationalPoint(0, -34839094706, 0), seg-000125 ep = RationalPoint(0, 1791925913988, 0).

bugs.error_message: simplex::tests::get_instance_sort_is_stable_for_equal_compare_to panicked: survivor 2 not found in input: Line { a: Int(774978817,1997027347), b: Int(774977195,1997025725) }
bugs.root_cause: Test-formulation bug, not a port bug: check (b) of the sort-stability invariant demanded the survivors form a greedy IN-ORDER subsequence of the input, but the generated fans use strides [0,1,3,2] mod 8 and therefore wrap — the input is NOT sorted, while Simplex.getInstance always outputs in compareTo order. Java never derives lines (Simplex.java:46-51 copies references, removeRedundantLines :884 only skips/shifts references), so the true contract is: endpoint-exact MEMBERSHIP in the input (order-free) + sorted output + ties (compareTo == Equal) keeping their input RELATIVE order (TimSort stability survives removal-only pruning). A doc-comment-only edit had also shifted the panic line number, initially masking that the failing code was unchanged.
bugs.fix: Replaced the greedy cursor with (b) input.iter().position endpoint-exact membership per survivor and (c) pairwise tie-order check: for output i<j with compare_to == Equal, first_pos[i] < first_pos[j]. Green over 10k seeded fans (0x5EED_C0DE_1234_567D). Lesson: when a panic message survives a fix byte-identical, diff the algorithm, not the line number.

Then .get(i).cloned().flatten() clones only the single stored shape.

bugs.root_cause: Layer -1 reused from the plain query rows; the with-clearance core derives its window growth from the per-layer matrix row maxima, so a negative layer indexes no row and yields 0.
bugs.fix: Both sides (index_corpus.rs + IndexOracle.java) now pass t_layer/sLayer for wc and check_shape rows; clear-tie wc cls-1 now returns both keepouts in tie order [[3,0],[2,0]] vs empty cls 0/2.

bugs.summary: M2 T10 contacts pin: pic trace 1372 corner assertion failed because the expected corner LIST was reconstructed from the M_PAIR narrative (assumed 2 corners) while the capture pins only first/last — the DSN wire is 3-corner (type protect = USER_FIXED, normalize no-op), so the port was right and the pin literal was inferred.
bugs.root_cause: Expected value came from narrative inference, not from a capture row — the exact violation the 'jar-captured values only' rule exists for; capture lines pin first/last for M_Y, the full corner list only for M_X.
bugs.fix: Re-pinned to exactly what the capture shows (first/last via M_Y row, full corners via M_X_CORNERS row); related: tests pinning absolute inserted ids 12..16 must replay the FULL spike insertion sequence since alloc_id is monotone (skipping A3/B3 shifted ids).

bugs.summary: M2 T11: CombineSpike B_TREE baseline diverged from the port's post-parse tree; misdiagnosed as insertAllBoardItems walking ascending (creation order) — switching the walk to ascending broke ALL 33 T9 index goldens (trees[i].lines sha256) on the very next gate.
bugs.root_cause: Java's `itemList` is NOT a list: UndoableObjects.java:21,37 backs it with a ConcurrentSkipListMap keyed by the Item, and Item.compareTo is other.id - id (Item.java:95-103), so the startReadObject walk (insertAllBoardItems :217-231, removeAllBoardItems :202-215, getAutorouteTree :163-170) yields DESCENDING id. The T11 capture exercised the OTHER path: the read inserts each item at creation (ascending on parsed boards) and CombineSpike never calls reinsertTreeItems. Two Java build orders, one port fill function — each oracle proved the opposite fix.
bugs.fix: Split the fills: insert_all_board_items restored to the descending ConcurrentSkipListMap walk (rebuild path: reinsert_tree_items / set_clearance_compensation_used / clearance_value_changed — matches the T9 goldens), new insert_items_creation_order replays the read path ascending (trace_ops fresh() and future read integration). get_autoroute_tree's bulk insert already descended correctly. Both oracles green simultaneously: 33/33 index goldens + 153 epic-board tests incl. the 31-row B_TREE pin.
